findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace `--json` in Plan step 3 and AC line 3 with rebar's actual structured-output selector `--output json` (`-o json`), and state explicitly which mutating verbs (if any) expose a structured-output channel — since the `--output json` profiles today cover only read/report commands, not the mutations this plan targets.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/output.py:5 — 'the legacy --json and --format=* flags were removed'
docs/output-schemas.md:10 — 'The legacy --json and --format=* flags were removed (pre-1.0).'
CHANGELOG.md:1381 — 'Standardize structured output on --output/-o (drop --json/--format)'
scripts/probe_rebar.py:466 — 'legacy ready --json rejected (removed)'

output.py profiles (reader/ready/report) apply structured output to READ/REPORT commands, not the mutating verbs this plan targets — so it is unverified that any mutation verb has a JSON channel to protect at all
findings.finding: Plan step 3 and AC line 3 assert a `--json` output mode ('Where a --json output mode exists', 'JSON output modes remain valid JSON'), but rebar's `--json` flag was removed pre-1.0 and replaced by the single canonical `--output`/`-o` selector (with `json` as a value).
scenarios: Author/tester writes a test asserting `link --json` stays valid JSON and finds the flag does not exist
The '--json never corrupts JSON output' guard is written against a channel that no mutating verb actually exposes
findings.suggested_fix: Reword step 3 / AC-3 to: 'confirmations must not appear on `--output json`/`-o json` output for any command that supports it; verify no mutating verb currently emits `--output json`, and if none do, drop the JSON-safety clause or scope it to the read/report commands that do.' Also confirm the new `-q` short flag does not collide with the existing `-o` selector.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that link_core/add_dependency and leaf.py tag/untag/comment widen their return to carry a wrote-vs-noop signal (e.g. an enum/flag) so the CLI can choose the confirmation vs already-X line from existing return data — reconciling AC-2 with the 'no new store reads' constraint.
evidence: Plan step 1: 'Reuse each command's existing result data — no new store reads to build the message.'
Plan step 2 / AC-2 require an explicit 'already linked ...' notice on the idempotent path
graph/_links.py:277 'return redirect_record' on no-op; :290 'return redirect_record' on write — both None unless redirected
leaf.py:106 tag() no-op returns None, identical to write path returning None
findings.finding: The plan's 'reuse existing result data — no new store reads' constraint is not satisfiable for the idempotent-no-op notice: the core functions return no wrote-vs-noop signal. add_dependency returns redirect_record (None) identically for a real LINK write and for an idempotent no-op (graph/_links.py:277 vs :290); link_core passes that through (link_revert.py:63); leaf.py tag()/untag()/comment() all return None and the no-op branch (tag_value in tags, leaf.py:106) returns identically to the write path. So the CLI cannot distinguish 'linked'/'tagged' from 'already linked'/'already tagged' from existing return data.
findings.location: Plan step 1 & 2; Acceptance criteria AC-1, AC-2
scenarios: Re-link of an identical active edge must print 'already linked ...' but link_core returns None (same as a fresh successful link)
Re-tag of an already-present tag must print 'already tagged ...' but tag() returns None (same as a fresh tag)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a plan step: each mutating *_core returns a small result object (or existing-dict field) indicating {wrote|noop} and the resulting-state facts the message needs; the CLI branches on it. Note that add_dependency's idempotent no-op branch (graph/_links.py) currently returns None indistinguishably from a real write and must be amended to signal the no-op.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'comment added ... (<n> comments)' example with the no-new-read rule: either drop the count from the confirmation, or have comment_core return the post-append count so no extra read is needed.
evidence: Plan step 1 example: 'comment added to <alias> (<n> comments)'
Plan step 1 constraint: 'no new store reads to build the message'
leaf.py comment() signature returns None; the append writes one COMMENT event and never counts existing comments
findings.finding: The example confirmation 'comment added to <alias> (<n> comments)' requires a comment count that comment() does not return (leaf.py:49-87 returns None); computing <n> requires reducing the ticket — a new store read — which the plan explicitly forbids.
scenarios: Building the '(<n> comments)' suffix forces a reduce_ticket read after the append, contradicting AC-1's 'no extra store read is performed to build it'
findings.suggested_fix: Either change the comment confirmation to a countless form (e.g. 'comment added to <alias>') or specify that comment_core returns the resulting comment count (derivable from the reduce it already performs, if any) so the CLI builds '(<n> comments)' without a second read.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the JSON-safety clause with the existing --output/-o (parse_output) convention and scope it to verbs that actually have a structured mode, rather than positing a new --json flag.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/output.py:50-57 defines the canonical --output/-o mode selector (PROFILES reader/ready/report; formats json/llm/text); there is no --json flag
search_files '--json' finds only src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:106 on 'bridge status', which is a READ, not a mutating verb
The mutating verbs route through _WRITES_FULL/_LIFECYCLE (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:114,125-142) and none is shown to accept --output/json today
findings.finding: The plan's JSON-safety clause names a '--json' output mode, but the codebase's structured-output convention is '--output'/'-o' via parse_output (PROFILES json/llm/text), and the mutating verbs in scope (link/unlink/comment/tag/edit/transition) do not currently expose any json output mode — so the clause both risks a divergent flag name and is partly hypothetical for verbs that have no structured channel.
findings.location: Plan step 3 ('Where a --json output mode exists') / AC line 3 ('JSON output modes remain valid JSON')
scenarios: Author wires a new --json flag on mutating verbs that diverges from the existing --output/-o convention, or writes JSON-safety guards for verbs that emit no structured output
findings.suggested_fix: Reword step 3 to reference the existing `--output`/`-o` machinery (`rebar._engine_support.output.parse_output`) and note that mutating verbs currently have no structured mode, so the guard applies only if/where one is added.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rename the plan's '--json' references to the actual '--output json' flag (default 'text') and point suppression/structured-field logic at each command's existing --output parsing.
evidence: Plan step 3: 'Where a --json output mode exists, confirmations stay off that channel…'
src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:652 uses '--output json' (fmt), :531 'parse --output'; src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:198,211 reference '--output json'
search for '--json' as a CLI flag yields no matches in src/rebar/_cli
findings.finding: The plan describes the JSON output channel as '--json', but the codebase's actual flag is '--output json' (with a 'text' default). The AC 'JSON output modes remain valid JSON' therefore targets a flag name that does not exist under that spelling.
findings.location: Plan step 3 and AC line 3 ('--json output mode' / 'JSON output modes remain valid JSON')
scenarios: Implementer wires suppression logic keyed on a nonexistent '--json' flag rather than the real '--output json' parsing seam
findings.suggested_fix: Replace '--json output mode' with '--output json' and note it is per-command (e.g., transition/reopen/grounding-info), not a single global flag.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Complete the inventory: explicitly enumerate ALL mutating CLI verbs in _WRITES_FULL/_DISPATCH_PRIMARY (add untag, set-verify-commands, attach-commits, idea, archive, delete, compact/compact-all, import, sign, scratch) and state per-verb whether each gets a confirmation line or is intentionally excluded.
evidence: Plan step 5: 'enumerate mutating CLI verbs (transition/link/unlink/comment/tag/edit/claim/reopen/set-file-impact/session-log/tracker-maintenance...)'
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:125-142 _WRITES_FULL includes untag, set-verify-commands, attach-commits, idea, archive (none named in the plan)
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:148 _DISPATCH_PRIMARY adds delete/scratch/compact; _IO adds import; _SIGNING adds sign — all mutating and unnamed
findings.finding: The inventory enumeration omits several mutating CLI verbs that live in the same dispatch sets (_WRITES_FULL / _DISPATCH_PRIMARY) the plan will touch: untag, set-verify-commands, attach-commits, idea, archive, and (arguably) delete, compact/compact-all, import, sign, scratch. The plan's '...' + 'apply uniformly' hedges acknowledge more exist, but leaving them unnamed makes the edit-set boundary ambiguous for the acceptance criterion 'Each mutating CLI verb prints a one-line stdout confirmation.'
findings.location: Plan step 5 (Inventory pass) and AC line 1
scenarios: Reviewer/implementer cannot tell whether untag/set-verify-commands/archive/idea are in-scope for the one-line confirmation, so some mutating verbs stay silent after the change ships
findings.suggested_fix: Cross-reference src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py _WRITES_FULL and the _DISPATCH_PRIMARY frozensets and list every mutating verb with its intended confirmation line (or an explicit 'excluded because …').

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default rule for confirmations under --json (e.g. suppress the human line and, if desired, expose it as a named structured field), rather than offering the executor an unranked either/or.
evidence: 'Where a --json output mode exists, confirmations stay off that channel or ride a structured field — never corrupt JSON output.'
findings.finding: Step 3 defers a per-verb design decision — for JSON output modes, confirmations either 'stay off that channel OR ride a structured field' — to the executor without stating which default applies.
scenarios: An executor reaching a verb with a --json mode must choose between suppress-vs-embed with no stated rule, producing inconsistent behavior across verbs
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one default: 'Under --json, suppress the human confirmation line entirely; do not add fields' — or specify the exact field name if embedding.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether a failed mutation must emit a clear error diagnostic on stderr (and add an AC exercising a failure path's stream), or explicitly scope failure-visibility out with rationale reconciling it against the Why.
evidence: Why: 'success, silent idempotent no-op, and swallowed failure are indistinguishable'
Plan step 4: 'errors unaffected' / 'Exit codes remain the programmatic contract, unchanged' — no requirement that a failed mutation surface a diagnostic line
No AC exercises the failure path's stderr output
findings.finding: The Why cites 'swallowed failure' as one of three indistinguishable outcomes motivating the change, but the Plan and ACs only specify success confirmations and idempotent no-op notices — the failure-visibility case (a clear error line on failure) is never addressed.
findings.location: Why (third indistinguishable outcome) vs Plan steps 1-4 / ACs
scenarios: A mutation fails (e.g. link to nonexistent target); agent sees empty stdout, no confirmation line, and must still infer failure from exit code — the exact swallowed-failure ambiguity the Why claims to fix
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 4 that failures emit a one-line error to stderr with nonzero exit, and add an AC asserting a captured-stderr error line on a known failing mutation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the quiet toggle should ride the existing config surface / -c override (or a single shared global-flag parser) rather than a new per-verb --quiet/-q, and justify a new global flag if kept.
evidence: src/rebar/_config_schema.py:317 display_mode config key + src/rebar/_config_sections.py:51 show an established typed config surface with a CLI override layer (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:477-494 '-c/--config … installs the highest-precedence cli layer')
No existing 'quiet' config key or -q CLI flag exists (search_files for 'quiet'/'-q' returns only git/ssh-keygen/pytest usages, none a rebar CLI flag)
kubectl parity is a plausible justification for a per-invocation flag, so this is a confirm-not-forbid point
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new global --quiet/-q flag without checking it against the existing config-layer surface (ticket.* config keys resolved through load_config with CLI>env>project>user precedence, plus the -c/--config override), risking config/flag-surface proliferation for the scripting-suppression toggle.
findings.location: Plan step 3 / AC line 3 ('--quiet suppresses confirmations')
scenarios: Author adds a bespoke -q parser per command instead of routing through the existing config/override machinery, creating N divergent suppression parsers

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly acknowledge the default stdout change as a justified breaking choice (agents are the primary operators) and note the opt-out (--quiet) / back-out path for existing scripted consumers.
evidence: Why: verbs currently 'exit 0 with empty stdout on success'
Plan step 3: '--quiet/-q global flag suppresses the confirmation (scripts)' — makes suppression opt-OUT, so existing scripts get new output by default
findings.finding: Changing previously-silent verbs to print by default is a behavior change to the stdout contract; existing scripts that parse or expect empty stdout break unless they adopt --quiet, but the plan does not treat this as an explicit compat choice with a back-out/opt-in consideration.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (--quiet) and Why (Unix silence rule being abandoned)
scenarios: A caller script pipes `rebar link ...` stdout into a downstream parser expecting emptiness; after this change it receives an unexpected confirmation line
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line compat note: 'This flips previously-silent verbs to print by default (opt-out via --quiet); justified because agents are the primary operators and cannot see writes otherwise; scripts adopt --quiet.'
